observed_failure.last_started_step: Install pinned PDF and TeX toolchains
observed_failure.interpretation: The uploaded PDFs are the checkout's pre-existing bytes. No regression test, clean rebuild, clipping audit, or byte-equality gate executed, so the artifact carries no clean-render authority.

question: Can the exact pinned Ubuntu 24.04 PDF/TeX toolchain be installed under a bounded, observable protocol and then cleanly rebuild, geometry-audit, and byte-compare all fifteen manuscripts without changing scientific sources or clipping baselines?

forbidden_paths_and_classes: scientific results, claims, authorities, manuscripts, bibliographies, figures, or PDFs
P1 finalizer, Slurm, LUNARC, custody, integrity, and immutable-OID paths

installation_observability: Remove `-qq` from the result-bearing apt install so package progress and the last active package are retained.
Emit disk, memory, dpkg-lock-holder, apt-cache policy, and package-state diagnostics before installation.
Wrap apt update and apt install in separate explicit bounded commands; timeout must return a typed failure and may not fall through to render steps.
Use Acquire::Retries and bounded HTTP/HTTPS timeouts; do not silently retry forever.
Persist apt stdout/stderr, package candidate versions, installed versions, elapsed duration, and exit status as artifacts.
exact_toolchain: Retain the exact package set and exact version table already frozen in the workflow unless a candidate version is unavailable on the same ubuntu-24.04 image.
If an exact version is unavailable, return RENDER_TOOLCHAIN_VERSION_UNAVAILABLE; do not substitute another TeX distribution or image in this packet.
Record the runner image, image version, kernel, Python, pip package hashes, dpkg package versions, latexmk version, pdfTeX version, and poppler version.
execution_separation: Toolchain installation must complete and verify before tests or manuscript builds begin.
The 15 entry-point denominator must be computed before the first build and retained in a manifest.
Each manuscript build must have its own bounded command, source epoch, exit status, log SHA-256, PDF SHA-256, and duration so one hung manuscript is identifiable.
Run the clipping regression unit tests before the 15 builds.
Run geometry audit and tracked-PDF equality only after all 15 clean builds succeed.
artifact_integrity: The always-upload step must include a machine-readable stage-status ledger that distinguishes PREEXISTING_CHECKOUT_PDF from CLEAN_REBUILT_PDF.
A cancelled or failed build must never upload a pre-existing PDF under a name implying a clean rebuild.
Upload apt logs, toolchain manifest, entry-point manifest, per-paper build logs, per-paper build receipts, geometry report, and byte-diff report.
The final binding packet must SHA-256 every uploaded file and state whether clean-render authority was earned.

workflow_replay: Push only the workflow/development-packet repair to the required Codex branch.
Open or update the PR against the same base and execute `manuscript-clipping-audit` on the exact resulting head.
Do not import PDFs or logs from the cancelled run as rebuilt outputs.

If the exact toolchain installation times out again, retain diagnostics and return the typed resource terminal rather than raising the global timeout or replacing the toolchain without a successor freeze.

requirements: Exact pinned toolchain installation succeeds and every frozen package version matches.
Exactly 15 current manuscript entry points are found.
Exactly 15 clean builds succeed under their frozen SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH values.
No undefined citation/reference warning is retained.
Geometry audit returns zero new clipping and zero stale baseline rows.
All 15 tracked main.pdf files are byte-identical to the clean rebuild.
Every stage and artifact is content-bound; no pre-existing PDF is mislabeled as rebuilt.
